standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the analogous statement for the second assertion, after inverting an element of the base.

core_obligations: First assertion: by the localisation lemma the naive cotangent complex of S_g over R is the base change of that of S over R, which is assumed to be the finite projective module of differentials, and base change preserves finite projectivity, so S_g is smooth over R (proof lines 37338-37343).
Second assertion: the same argument with the base-localisation lemma, inverting an element f of R, gives smoothness of R_f -> S (proof lines 37345-37346).
proof_roadmap: Transport the naive cotangent complex along the localisation and read smoothness off finite projectivity (proof lines 37338-37343).
Repeat the argument for the base change by inverting f in R (proof lines 37345-37346).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a smooth ring map R -> S stays smooth after localizing the source (S_g over R) and after inverting in the base (R_f -> S) (statement lines 37329-37335). The proof does not compute with presentations: it uses the naive cotangent complex, transports it along the localization through the cited localisation lemma, and observes that finite projectivity - which is what smoothness of R -> S supplies - is preserved by base change (proof lines 37338-37343); the second assertion is the same argument with the base-localisation lemma (proof lines 37345-37346). The step that carries the content is the transport of the complex, since it is what turns the assumption on S into the corresponding statement for S_g and R_f. Both cited inputs are same-chapter lemmas. H2.
